title: Lesson 8. Save and find
description: Save a file into your folder, close it and find it again

questions.prompt: Put the saving steps in order
questions.explain: First where, then the name, then Save.

questions.prompt: Notepad text saves itself even if you close without saving.
questions.explain: You must save, or the text is lost.

questions.prompt: Where do you type the file name when saving?
options: In the "File name" box at the bottom
questions.explain: The "File name" box at the bottom of the window.

questions.prompt: Match the picture with the meaning
questions.explain: Saving = putting the notebook in the schoolbag.

questions.prompt: How do you open a saved file again?
questions.explain: Find the folder and double-click the file.

questions.prompt: After Ctrl + S you don't need to choose the folder again.
questions.explain: The computer already knows where the file is.

questions.prompt: What do we do if we closed without saving by accident?
questions.explain: No worries — it teaches why saving matters.

learn.intro: The most important lesson of the course! We learn to save and find our work — grown-ups often can't.

slides.text: While you type in Notepad, the text only lives on the screen — like chalk on a board. Close the program — the board is wiped.
To keep the text forever you **save** it — put the notebook in the schoolbag.

check.prompt: If you close Notepad without saving, the text is lost.
check.explain: The board was wiped — no text.

slides.text: Menu **File → Save As**. A window opens. The key thing is to look **where** we save: Documents → your folder.
At the bottom is the "File name" box — type, for example, **My games**, and press **Save**.
The main question: **where am I saving?** If you don't know — you won't find it later.

check.prompt: What is the main question when saving?
check.explain: Otherwise you won't find the file later.

slides.text: The "Find your notebook" game: close Notepad → File Explorer → Documents → your folder → double-click the file. Hooray, the notebook is there!
Added more? Press **Ctrl + S** — quick save. No need to pick a folder: the computer already knows where the file is.
